name: Real estate teams
short: Every new lead answered in under a minute, qualified, and booked for a viewing or call.
title: AI automation for real estate teams
description: Done-for-you AI automations for real estate teams: portal and website leads answered in about a minute, qualified, and booked for a viewing or a call.
headline: A lead that arrives at 11pm should not wait until 9am
lede: We set up an assistant that replies to every portal, website and WhatsApp enquiry in about a minute, asks the questions your ISA would ask, and puts the viewing in an agent's calendar. Your agents start the day with booked appointments, not a list of people to chase.

hero.title: Tuesday night, a portal enquiry

events.text: A buyer asks about a three-bed listing through a property portal.
Replies by text and email: the home is available. Asks about budget, timing and financing.
Buyer answers: pre-approved, wants to move within three months.
Offers two slots from the listing agent's calendar. Buyer picks Thursday, 5:30pm.
Lead, answers and viewing saved to the CRM. Agent notified.
Agent reads the summary over coffee and confirms the viewing by phone.

hero.footer: Enquiry to booked viewing: about a minute

pains.lede: None of this is hard work. It is work that arrives at the wrong time.

items.title: Portal leads go cold overnight
items.text: Enquiries from listing portals arrive in the evening and at weekends. By the time someone replies the next morning, the buyer has often messaged other agents.

items.title: Agents qualify by hand
items.text: Every new lead means the same questions about budget, timing, area and financing, typed out between viewings.

items.title: Viewings booked by back-and-forth
items.text: Finding a slot takes several messages, and the no-shows are the ones nobody reminded.

items.title: The CRM is a week behind
items.text: Notes live in phones and inboxes, so the Monday pipeline meeting runs on memory.

automations.lede: Each one is a separate piece. Start with the first, add the others when it has earned its keep.

flow.title: Main workflow: new enquiry to booked viewing

items.name: Instant lead reply
items.trigger: A new enquiry from a listing portal, your website form, WhatsApp or a missed call.
items.does: Replies in about a minute by text, email or WhatsApp, in your team's tone, with the details of the listing they asked about.
items.person: Nothing, unless the buyer asks for a person. Then it hands over with the conversation attached.

items.name: Lead qualification
items.trigger: The buyer or seller replies.
items.does: Asks the questions your ISA would ask: budget, timing, area, financing, whether they have a home to sell. Writes a short summary and a priority.
items.person: Agents read the summary and decide who to call first.

items.name: Viewing booking and reminders
items.trigger: A qualified lead wants to see a property.
items.does: Offers free slots from the agent's calendar, books the viewing, and sends a reminder the day before and an hour before.
items.person: The agent shows the home.

items.name: CRM logging and lead routing
items.trigger: Any new lead or booked viewing.
items.does: Creates or updates the contact, attaches the conversation, and assigns the lead by area, price band or round-robin.
items.person: The team lead sets the routing rules and can change them at any time.

items.name: Long-term follow-up
items.trigger: A lead says not yet, or goes quiet.
items.does: Checks in on a schedule you approve, with new listings that match what they asked for.
items.person: An agent picks up as soon as the lead replies.

worth.lede: A worked example for a small brokerage. Swap in your own lead volume and commission and the sum changes with them.
assumptions: 40 new leads a month from portals and your website
15 minutes of agent time per lead today on the first reply and the basic questions
Agent time costed at $40 an hour
One extra deal a quarter from leads that used to go unanswered overnight
An average commission to the brokerage of $6,000

That time, valued at $40 an hour

items.title: It says it is an assistant
items.text: Messages make clear the buyer is talking to an automated assistant for your team, and offer a person at any point.

items.title: It stays inside the listing
items.text: The assistant answers from your listing data and the rules you set. It does not negotiate, quote a price that is not on the listing, or give legal or mortgage advice.

items.title: Fair housing and local rules
items.text: Qualifying questions are written with you and limited to budget, timing and property needs. You review the script against the fair housing and advertising rules that apply where you work before it goes live.

items.title: Consent for texts and calls
items.text: Rules on texting and calling leads differ by country and state. We build in opt-out handling and quiet hours, and you confirm the consent wording for your market.

items.title: You own the accounts
items.text: The CRM, phone number, WhatsApp account and workflow accounts are in your name. If we stop working together, everything keeps running.

items.q: Will buyers know they are talking to an AI?
items.a: Yes. The first message says it is the team's assistant, and anyone can ask for a person. Late at night, a clear answer and a time slot is usually what the enquiry was for.

items.q: What happens when a lead asks something it cannot answer?
items.a: It says so, takes the question, and passes the conversation to the right agent with a summary. It does not guess at prices, offers or legal points.

items.q: We already have an ISA. Does this replace them?
items.a: No. It covers the hours and the volume a person cannot, and does the first reply and the basic questions. Your ISA spends their time on the calls that need a person.

items.q: Does it work with our CRM and portals?
items.a: If your CRM has an API, a Zapier or Make connection, or can receive email, almost certainly. Portal leads usually arrive by email or a feed, which is enough. We check your exact setup in the audit before quoting.

items.q: How long before it is live?
items.a: A first pilot, usually instant reply and qualification for one lead source, takes two to four weeks including a test period on real enquiries.

pilot.lede: Start with the one lead source that loses the most enquiries. Prove it on real leads, then decide whether to add the rest.
scope: Instant reply and qualification for one lead source, such as your main portal or website form
Viewing booking into one shared calendar or one per agent
Every conversation logged to your CRM with a summary
A weekly report: leads answered, qualified, booked and handed to a person

timeline.text: Access, your qualifying questions, reply wording and routing rules agreed.
Built and tested on past enquiries. Your team tries to break it.
Live on real leads with daily checks, then a review of the numbers together.

name: Clinics and dental practices
short: An AI receptionist on WhatsApp and the phone, with reminders that cut no-shows.
title: AI receptionist for clinics and dental practices
description: An AI receptionist for clinics and dental practices: bookings on WhatsApp and the phone, appointment reminders, patient recall, and urgent cases passed to staff.
linkLabel: See the clinics and dental page
headline: The phone rings while your front desk is with a patient
lede: We set up a receptionist on WhatsApp and the phone that books, reschedules and reminds, day and night. Hygiene recalls go out on time, gaps in the diary are offered to the waiting list, and anything clinical or urgent goes straight to your team.

messages.text: Hi, I need a check-up and a clean. Anything next week?
Hello, this is the practice's booking assistant. For a check-up with a hygiene appointment I have Tuesday at 8:30am or Thursday at 4:15pm. Which suits you?
Booked: Thursday, 4:15pm, check-up and hygiene. I will remind you the day before.
Reminder: your appointment is tomorrow at 4:15pm. Reply 1 to confirm or 2 to change it.

pains.lede: A front desk has one pair of hands. These are the jobs that lose out.

items.title: Calls go unanswered at the busiest times
items.text: The front desk is checking a patient in, taking a payment and answering the phone at once. A caller who gets voicemail may simply book somewhere else.

items.title: Reminders are done by hand, or not at all
items.text: Someone works through tomorrow's list by phone when there is a quiet half hour. On a busy day there is none, and the no-shows follow.

items.title: Recalls slip
items.text: Patients due a check-up or hygiene appointment sit in a report nobody has time to work through.

items.title: Cancellations leave gaps
items.text: A late cancellation leaves an empty chair, even though there are patients who wanted an earlier slot.

automations.lede: You can start with reminders and recalls only, and add booking once you trust it.

flow.title: Main workflow: message to confirmed appointment

nodes.label: Reminds and confirms
nodes.sub: Two days and two hours before

items.name: WhatsApp and phone booking
items.trigger: A patient messages or calls, at any hour.
items.does: Answers, finds a slot in your practice management system for the right appointment type and clinician, books it and confirms in writing.
items.person: The front desk handles anything unusual. Clinical questions and complaints go to them with the conversation attached.

items.name: Appointment reminders
items.trigger: A set time before each appointment, such as two days and two hours.
items.does: Sends a reminder with a one-tap confirm or reschedule. Unconfirmed appointments are flagged for a call.
items.person: Staff call only the patients who did not confirm.

items.name: Patient recall
items.trigger: A patient becomes due for a check-up, hygiene appointment or review.
items.does: Sends a recall message with available slots, follows up on a schedule you set, and books the reply.
items.person: You set who is recalled and when. The assistant never changes a recall interval a clinician has set.

items.name: Cancellation and waiting-list fill
items.trigger: An appointment is cancelled or moved.
items.does: Offers the freed slot to patients on the waiting list who wanted that kind of appointment. The first to reply gets it.
items.person: The front desk approves the list rules, such as who is offered short-notice slots.

items.name: Urgent case handover
items.trigger: A message or call mentions pain, swelling, bleeding, an injury or anything else on your urgent list.
items.does: Stops the booking conversation, gives your emergency instructions, and alerts the member of staff on duty straight away.
items.person: A clinician or trained member of staff decides what happens next. The assistant never assesses symptoms.

worth.lede: A worked example for a practice with a few chairs. Your diary, fees and no-show numbers will be different, so treat this as the shape of the sum.
assumptions: 600 booked appointments a month across the practice
30 of them missed without notice today, with reminders and one-tap rescheduling saving 12
6 patients a month who message after closing now book, where before they heard nothing until morning
An average appointment worth $150
15 hours a month of reminder and booking calls handed back to the front desk, at $22 an hour
worth.setupNote: One-off setup in this example: $4,500, covered in the third month.

items.title: No medical advice
items.text: The assistant books, reminds and answers practical questions such as opening hours, parking and what to bring. It does not assess symptoms, suggest treatment or comment on medication.

items.title: Urgent cases go to a person
items.text: You give us the words and situations that count as urgent. When one comes up, the assistant stops, gives your emergency instructions and alerts your team.

items.title: Patient data is agreed per project
items.text: Which data the assistant can see, where it is processed and how long it is kept are written down before anything is built. If your practice falls under HIPAA or UK GDPR, the tools, agreements and hosting are chosen with you to fit, and you confirm them with your own compliance adviser.

items.title: It says it is an assistant
items.text: Patients are told they are talking to an automated assistant and can ask for a member of staff at any point.

items.title: You own the accounts
items.text: The phone number, WhatsApp account and workflow accounts belong to the practice.

items.q: Is it safe to let an AI talk to patients?
items.a: It is limited to booking, reminders and practical questions, and it is told what it must not do. Anything clinical, urgent or upset goes to your team with the conversation attached. You read and approve every script before it goes live.

items.q: What about HIPAA or UK GDPR?
items.a: It depends on your practice and the tools involved, so we agree it in writing per project: what data is used, where it is processed and which agreements are needed. We will tell you plainly if a tool you want cannot be used the way your rules require.

items.q: Does it work with our practice management system?
items.a: If your system offers an API or an approved integration, the assistant can read free slots and write bookings directly. If it does not, there are slower routes, such as a shared booking calendar that staff confirm. We check this first, in the audit.

items.q: Can we start small?
items.a: Yes. Reminders and recalls alone are a sensible first step, because they touch no clinical decisions. Booking by WhatsApp or phone can be added later. The assistant is always clear about what it is, and a person is one message away.

items.q: Can it answer the phone, or only WhatsApp?
items.a: Both. The voice line can answer every call, or only the ones your front desk cannot pick up within a few rings. Each call is summarised in writing so staff can see what was booked.

pilot.lede: Reminders and recall make a good first project. They touch no clinical decisions, and the result shows up in the diary.

name: Agencies and B2B sales teams
short: Meeting notes into the CRM and follow-ups sent, without anyone typing them up.
title: AI automation for agencies and B2B sales teams
description: For agencies and B2B sales teams: call notes written for you, the CRM updated after every meeting, and the follow-up drafted before the next call starts.
linkLabel: See the agencies and sales teams page
headline: Your pipeline is only as good as last week's call notes
lede: We connect your meetings to your CRM. When a call ends, the notes are written, the deal is updated, next steps become tasks and the follow-up email is waiting as a draft. Reps review and send. Nobody types up a call again.

hero.title: Thursday, after a discovery call

events.text: Call with a prospect ends. Recording and transcript are ready.
Writes the call notes: goals, budget, who decides, objections, agreed next steps.
Updates the deal in the CRM: stage, amount, close date and three tasks with owners.
Drafts the follow-up email with the recap and the proposal date.
Rep reads the draft, changes one line and sends it.

hero.footer: Call ended to follow-up sent: 7 minutes

pains.lede: Selling is the job. This is the part that crowds it out.

items.title: Notes get written at 6pm, or never
items.text: After five calls in a day, the details of the first one are gone. What reaches the CRM is one line.

items.title: The CRM does not match reality
items.text: Stages, amounts and close dates are updated the night before the pipeline review, so the forecast is a guess.

items.title: Follow-ups go out late
items.text: The recap email waits behind the next call, and the prospect's interest cools while it does.

items.title: Handovers lose the detail
items.text: When a deal moves from sales to delivery, or from one rep to another, what the client actually said stays in someone's head.

automations.lede: Everything lands where your team already works: the deal record, the task list and the drafts folder.

flow.title: Main workflow: call ended to follow-up ready

items.name: Call notes
items.trigger: A recorded video or phone call ends.
items.does: Writes structured notes in your format: needs, budget, decision makers, objections, competitors mentioned and next steps.
items.person: The rep skims the notes and corrects anything the recording got wrong.

items.name: CRM update
items.trigger: The notes are ready.
items.does: Finds the right contact and deal, updates stage, amount and close date, fills the fields you care about, and creates tasks with owners and due dates.
items.person: For changes you mark as sensitive, such as amount or stage, the rep approves with one click before it saves.

items.name: Follow-up draft
items.trigger: The CRM update is done.
items.does: Drafts the recap email in the rep's own style, with the agreed next steps and any promised documents listed.
items.person: The rep edits and sends. Nothing goes to a client without a person pressing send.

items.name: CRM hygiene sweep
items.trigger: Every Monday morning, or a schedule you choose.
items.does: Lists deals with no next step, close dates in the past, missing amounts and contacts with no owner, and sends each rep their own short list.
items.person: Reps fix their list. The sales lead sees what is still open.

items.name: Sales-to-delivery handover
items.trigger: A deal is marked won.
items.does: Builds a brief from every call and email on the deal: what was sold, what was promised, who is who, and the risks raised.
items.person: The account lead reads it before the kickoff call.

worth.lede: A worked example for a six-person team. It counts admin time only, which is the part you can measure in the first month.
assumptions: 6 reps or account leads
10 client or prospect calls each a week, about 240 a month
12 minutes a call today on notes, the CRM and the follow-up
3 minutes a call to review what the automation prepared
A loaded cost of $50 an hour
worth.setupNote: One-off setup in this example: $3,000, covered in the third month. Not counted: deals that stop slipping because the follow-up went out the same day.

items.title: Recording needs consent
items.text: Call recording rules differ by country and state. The recorder announces itself, and you decide which calls are recorded and how participants are told.

items.title: A person sends every email
items.text: Follow-ups are drafts. Nothing goes to a client or prospect until a rep has read it and pressed send.

items.title: Sensitive fields need approval
items.text: You choose which CRM changes save automatically and which wait for a click, so the forecast is never rewritten without the rep seeing it.

items.title: Your data stays in your accounts
items.text: Recordings, transcripts and notes live in your own CRM and storage, and how long they are kept is your setting. Confidentiality terms you have signed with clients are checked before any call is processed.

items.title: You own the accounts
items.text: The CRM, the recorder and the workflow accounts are in your company's name. If we stop working together, everything keeps running.

items.q: Are the notes accurate enough to trust?
items.a: They are good on what was said and agreed, and weaker on names, numbers and strong accents, which is why the rep reviews before anything is sent. In the pilot we compare the notes against a sample of calls with you, and tune the format until your team would rather edit them than write their own.

items.q: Does this need a bot in every meeting?
items.a: Not always. If your meeting tool already records, the automation can work from that recording. Where a notetaker joins the call, it announces itself. You choose which meetings are covered.

items.q: We tried a notetaker app and nobody used it. Why is this different?
items.a: A summary that sits in a separate app is one more place to look. This puts the result where the work already happens: the deal record, the task list and the drafts folder. Reps do less, not one more thing.

items.q: Can it follow our sales method?
items.a: Yes. If you qualify with a set of questions, such as budget, authority, need and timing, the notes and CRM fields follow that structure, and the hygiene sweep flags deals where an answer is missing.

items.q: What about calls with confidential client details?
items.a: You can exclude clients, meeting types or individual calls. Recordings and notes stay in your own accounts, and we agree retention and access in writing before the build.

pilot.lede: Start with one team and one call type. New-business discovery calls are a good choice, because a missed follow-up there costs the most.

name: Bookkeeping firms
short: Invoices and bank lines matched automatically, with only the exceptions left for a person.
title: AI automation for bookkeeping firms
description: For bookkeeping firms: bank feeds matched to invoices and receipts automatically, missing documents chased for you, and only the exceptions left for a person.
headline: Month-end should be the exceptions, not every line
lede: We set up matching that reads each bank line, finds the invoice, bill or receipt, and proposes the entry with its reasoning. Your team approves the routine in batches and spends its time on the lines that need judgement. Nothing posts to a client's ledger without review unless you choose that.

rows.label: Bank lines imported from the feed
Matched to an invoice, bill or receipt
rows.note: Amount, date and reference all agree

rows.label: Matched by a rule you approved
Exceptions left for a person
rows.note: 6 missing receipts, 5 part payments, 4 unknown payees

pains.lede: The judgement is the valuable part of the job. The matching is what eats the week.

items.title: Bank feeds that still need a person on every line
items.text: Bank rules catch the obvious. The rest is someone clicking through lines, one client at a time.

items.title: Chasing clients for receipts and invoices
items.text: The same emails, to the same clients, every month, and the close waits for the replies.

items.title: Month-end piles up
items.text: Coding and matching are left until the last week, so the close runs late and the team works evenings to get it out.

items.title: Senior time spent on junior work
items.text: The people who should be reviewing and advising are keying supplier bills.

automations.lede: It works alongside the bank rules you already have, and every proposal shows why it was made.

flow.title: Main workflow: bank line to reviewed entry

items.name: Bank line matching
items.trigger: New lines arrive on a client's bank feed.
items.does: Matches each line to an open invoice, bill or receipt by amount, date, reference and payee, and proposes the entry with a confidence score and its reason.
items.person: A bookkeeper approves proposed matches in batches and works the exceptions.

items.name: Bill and receipt capture
items.trigger: A client emails, uploads or photographs a document.
items.does: Reads the supplier, date, amounts and tax, suggests the account code from that client's history, and attaches the document to the entry.
items.person: Anything new, unclear or over a limit you set waits for review.

items.name: Missing-document chaser
items.trigger: A bank line has no document after a number of days you choose.
items.does: Sends the client one tidy list of what is missing, with a link to upload, and reminds them on your schedule.
items.person: The client manager steps in for clients who do not respond.

items.name: Exceptions queue
items.trigger: A line cannot be matched or breaks a rule, such as a duplicate, a part payment or an unknown payee.
items.does: Puts it in one queue per client with the likely explanation and the nearest candidates.
items.person: A bookkeeper decides. Their decision can become a rule for next time, if they approve it.

items.name: Month-end close checklist
items.trigger: The last working day of the month, or your own close calendar.
items.does: Checks each client for unreconciled lines, open exceptions, missing documents and unusual balances, and sends the status to the client manager.
items.person: The reviewer signs off the close.

worth.lede: A worked example for a small firm. It only counts the lines your existing bank rules do not already catch.
assumptions: 2,400 bank lines a month, across your clients, that bank rules do not match
2 minutes a line by hand today
A match proposed for 1,800 of them, approved in batches at about 20 seconds each
600 exceptions that still take 2 minutes each
Bookkeeper time costed at $35 an hour
worth.setupNote: One-off setup in this example: $4,000, covered in the fifth month. Not counted: the extra clients that 50 hours a month would let you take on without hiring.

items.title: A person approves exceptions
items.text: The automation proposes. A bookkeeper decides anything that is not a clean match, and can see why each match was suggested.

items.title: Nothing posts unreviewed unless you choose
items.text: By default every entry waits for approval. If you decide that certain clean matches may post automatically for a client, that is your written rule, with limits, and it can be switched off.

items.title: Every entry has a trail
items.text: Each proposed and approved entry records the source document, the reason for the match and who approved it.

items.title: Client data stays in your systems
items.text: The work runs through your accounting software's own access controls. Which data leaves it, where it is processed and for how long are agreed in writing first.

items.title: Not tax or accounting advice
items.text: The automation does matching and chasing. Treatment, judgement and sign-off stay with your qualified staff.

items.q: How is this different from the bank rules in our accounting software?
items.a: Bank rules match on fixed text. This reads the document as well as the line, so it can handle references that change, part payments, batched payouts and suppliers it has not seen in that exact form. It works alongside your existing rules and leaves them in place.

items.q: Can it post entries by itself?
items.a: Only if you choose that, client by client, for the kinds of match you define. The default is that everything waits for a bookkeeper to approve.

items.q: What happens when it gets one wrong?
items.a: Proposed matches show their reason, so a wrong one is quick to spot and reject. Rejections are logged and used to adjust the rules. In the pilot we measure how many proposals your team accepts unchanged before anything is widened.

items.q: How do you get access to client ledgers?
items.a: Through a user or app connection that you create and control in your accounting software, limited to the clients in scope. You can remove it at any time. We do not hold client bank logins.

items.q: Does it handle multi-currency and sales tax or VAT?
items.a: It reads currency and tax amounts from the documents and proposes the tax code from each client's history. Unusual treatments go to the exceptions queue for a person.

pilot.lede: Start with a handful of clients who have high transaction volume and tidy documents, so the result is easy to measure.

A weekly report: lines proposed, approved unchanged, corrected and left as exceptions
